ARTECO · WP1 data inventory · compiled 27 September 2026

Anaktuvuk River Fire — In-situ & Near-ground Field-Data Inventory

What ground, tower and low-altitude (foot / helicopter / airborne-LiDAR) measurements exist at the 2007 Anaktuvuk River Fire (ARF) scar, who holds them, and whether they are publicly downloadable — mapped to what WP1–WP4 need (energy / water / carbon fluxes, soil-thermal state & active layer, vegetation succession and fire severity). Scope is deliberately narrow: only data with a real spatial footprint inside the ARF scar, and only variables that feed a work package. No satellite-only products, and no off-topic field records.

Section 1

In-situ field experiments, grouped by lead collaborator (data holder)

Every lane below is a ground, hand-held, tower or foot/helicopter-access measurement campaign at the Anaktuvuk River Fire (ARF) — no satellite imagery or satellite-derived index is charted. Light lanes = long-term background monitoring; solid lanes = the intensive field campaign. Two isolated visit years are drawn as two separate short ticks, not one connecting bar. The ruler stays fixed while you scroll.

🟢 green = directly public / confirmed downloadable 🟡 amber = partially public (some variables released, others not) ⚪ grey = no data-access link given in the paper 🔴 red = no public dataset found
Lane color = measurement type: Vegetation / burn severity Soil / permafrost / active layer Micrometeorology / flux / radiation Biogeochemistry / molecular

Section 2

Public / archived data products — grouped by where they sit

Reusable, downloadable packages of ARF field measurements, sorted into groups (towers → permafrost → transects → regional). Each product shows the variables it carries, its temporal resolution and location, and a coverage bar with dates. Off-topic records (small-mammal / herbivory) and non-Anaktuvuk-only products are excluded. There are 10 cards below; the source list numbers 12 data products, because [11] TRY (global trait database, request-based) and [12] Umiat USGS station (auxiliary nearby station) are numbered sources but carry no ARF product card of their own.

Variable theme: Energy Carbon / GPP Vegetation Soil Permafrost Fire

Section 3

What we can actually pull, by data type

A many-to-many crosswalk: each data type is served by one or more sources of record, and each source carries several variables. Where a PI campaign (Section 1) is also archived publicly (Section 2), they are merged and the public product is quoted. ARF-direct = measured inside the scar; regional = Alaska/ABoVE product to be filtered to ARF. The Feeds column names what each source supports (energy, vegetation, …) instead of a WP number.

Sources

Numbered sources

The light-grey number by each source points here — same number = same source. Data products [1–12] were each checked live against its landing page (✓ verified). Papers [13–28] are the Section-1 citations (held in our Redis library); each notes where its data is archived (→ [n]).

Data products [1–12]

  1. 1 AmeriFlux ARF towers — US-An1 severe / US-An2 moderate / US-An3 unburned. ameriflux.lbl.gov. ✓ site names confirmed; towers listed 2008–Present (CC-BY, free registration); latest years direct from Rocha.
  2. 2 Arctic Data Center A2251FM9P (Jones et al.) — repeat LiDAR + ground temperature + boreholes. doi 10.18739/A2251FM9P. ✓ files, CC0, 2009–2023 confirmed.
  3. 3 ORNL DAAC 2119 — ABoVE post-fire & unburned BLM field sites. doi 10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2119. ✓ 26 transects, 2008–2017, cover/density/thaw/soil confirmed (no dNBR variable).
  4. 4 EDI — ARF thaw-depth (Rocha & Shaver). knb-lter-arc.10123.6. ✓ 2008-06 → 2014-09, 3 towers, ~70 pts/site.
  5. 5 EDI — ARF eddy-flux, per site/year. knb-lter-arc.10345–10348 + 20115 (unburned 2013–19). ✓ ½-hourly NEE + energy.
  6. 6 EDI — Mack carbon/nitrogen-loss (series 10124–10127); best single knb-lter-arc.10126.5. ✓ organic-layer, C:N, combusted C, dNBR.
  7. 7 EDI — Bret-Harte biomass & soil N (series knb-lter-arc.10198–10204). ✓ above + root biomass, C:N, 2011, 6 transects.
  8. 8 EDI — N×P fertilization LAI knb-lter-arc.20108.2 (+ point-frame 20106.2, canopy 20137.1). ✓ 2016–2019.
  9. 9 ORNL DAAC 1903 — "Soil Moisture & ALT in Alaska and NWT, 2008–2020". doi …/1903. ✓ regional — filter to ARF coords.
  10. 10 ORNL DAAC 2177 — SATFiD "…Alaska Tundra Sites, 1972–2020", 37 datasets. doi …/2177. ✓ ALT / soil / PFT cover / fire history (no LAI or biomass); isolate ARF rows via dataset-ID.
  11. 11 TRY plant-trait database — global, request-based. try-db.org. ✓ SLA / height / rooting depth are standard; leaf-toughness is not a TRY trait — request Fetcher (2021) data from authors.
  12. 12 Umiat USGS station (AK104) — snow depth / soil moisture, hourly. USGS DS 1021. ✓ 1998–2015 (not 2004→present); hourly file direct-download.

Section 4

GEE satellite & reanalysis time series at the three flux sites

Multi-year Google Earth Engine series extracted at the three AmeriFlux / Rocha towers (US-An1 severe · US-An2 moderate · US-An3 unburned), with the AmeriFlux growing-season flux windows shaded so the remote-sensing and reanalysis curves line up with when the towers actually measured. These complement the in-situ inventory above with continuous, downloadable spatial context (GPP, NIRv, VPD, soil temperature, energy balance, recovery trajectories).

US-An1 severe US-An2 moderate US-An3 unburned AmeriFlux flux period (2008–2019 growing seasons) 2007 fire
How to read these (method):
  • US-An1 / An2 / An3 = the value of the single GEE pixel over each tower through time (image.sampleRegions, no spatial averaging). MODIS/Landsat (250 m–1 km) resolve the three towers → three coloured lines; ERA5-Land (~11 km) can't → drawn as one dark line (the towers share the same cells, see Fig F).
  • Blue bands = "growing season": the snow-free months each year (≈ May/Jun–Aug/Sep) when the eddy-covariance towers actually record fluxes; the public AmeriFlux BASE record spans 2008–2019. Compare the curves inside the bands when relating to the tower fluxes.
  • x-axis ticks every year (rotated 24°), 2000–2026; VPD from ERA5 2 m temperature & dew point (Tetens); energy _sum J m⁻² → W m⁻².
  • Underlying 20 CSVs and the full method write-up live in gee_csv/ (WP1_GEE_figures_and_methods.md); exports also in Google Drive ARF_ARTECO_WP1_GEE.

Deployment, team & source notesDetails for LT-001
Deployment notes
Sites were selected in late May 2008 (AmeriFlux / OSTI). Zipper et al. (2018) report instrument installation in June 2008.
Data coverage notes
Kim et al. (2026) use June–August NEE observations from 2008–2023. Earlier archives extend to 2019; newer annual files for 2020–2023 have not been checked individually. This is a seasonal series with gaps.
Location notes
Approximate station location converted from degrees–minutes–seconds in Jiang et al. (2015), Table 1. Individual probe positions are not listed. Some later papers label tower coordinates differently; the Table 1 convention is used here.
Team and institution
Initially The Ecosystems Center, Marine Biological Laboratory (MBL) / Arctic LTER; later work includes Rocha at the University of Notre Dame. John Hobbie is also listed among the AmeriFlux contributors.
Are installation participants named?
Installation participants are not named.
Related papers / documentation
Rocha & Shaver (2011), CO₂ exchange and energy exchange; Zipper et al. (2018); Kim et al. (2026)
Instrument and archive notes
AmeriFlux and EDI flux archives refer to the same physical towers. Radiation and meteorology are co-located components. Unburned controls retain their own setting label; a uniform fire-perimeter check has not been completed.
Operating status
Current operation has not been checked.

Deployment, team & source notesDetails for LT-003
Deployment notes
Sites were selected in late May 2008 (AmeriFlux / OSTI). Zipper et al. (2018) report instrument installation in June 2008.
Data coverage notes
Kim et al. (2026) use June–August NEE observations from 2008–2023. Earlier archives extend to 2019; newer annual files for 2020–2023 have not been checked individually. This is a seasonal series with gaps.
Location notes
Approximate station location converted from degrees–minutes–seconds in Jiang et al. (2015), Table 1. Individual probe positions are not listed. Some later papers label tower coordinates differently; the Table 1 convention is used here.
Team and institution
Initially The Ecosystems Center, Marine Biological Laboratory (MBL) / Arctic LTER; later work includes Rocha at the University of Notre Dame. John Hobbie is also listed among the AmeriFlux contributors.
Are installation participants named?
Installation participants are not named.
Related papers / documentation
Rocha & Shaver (2011), CO₂ exchange and energy exchange; Zipper et al. (2018); Kim et al. (2026)
Instrument and archive notes
AmeriFlux and EDI flux archives refer to the same physical towers. Radiation and meteorology are co-located components. Unburned controls retain their own setting label; a uniform fire-perimeter check has not been completed.
Operating status
Current operation has not been checked.

A few notes on dates and locations

Deployment and coverage are separate. An installation month, a first observation and an archive start describe different things. Each record keeps its original date type. The last reported data date does not imply removal.

Shared sites stay linked. Tower soil sensors belong to the three flux-tower sites. HOBO and SRS components share AKB / AKU. The EDI shallow-soil archive is retained separately while its hardware links are clarified.

Coordinates are station locations. Tower coordinates follow Jiang et al. (2015), Table 1; some later site labels differ. Exact northern logger and EDI-array GPS positions are not yet available. Fire-perimeter membership has not been checked uniformly.

Coverage is taken from the cited sources. Seasonal windows and known gaps are noted in each record. Raw-file completeness and current station operation have not been assessed. All downloads include the full register, regardless of active filters.

2007 marks the fire. The 2026 thaw-probing visit is included with a note on its year assignment. The 2027 block is reserved for future entries.

Included here: ARF-related field sampling, manual measurements, and individual airborne LiDAR acquisitions. Automated ground-temperature and flux-tower datasets remain in the dataset crosswalk.
Integrated entries: Stream-water sampling appears under 2017 and 2018, and Groome's thaw-probing visit under 2026. SATFiD links are attached to the original experiments. Stream sampling locations still need a point-by-point fire-perimeter check. The 2026 visit is assigned to that year by cross-referencing two sources; details are included in its row.

Fields for matching records
The official guide lists Tundra_field_database.csv、Dataset_List.csv、Method_Differences.csv. Match records using dataset_id, original plot ID, coordinates, and date. A zero for an unknown month or day remains an unknown date component. Field definitions
Regional soil-data reference
The first author of S18 is Yue Wu. The InSAR analysis masks out the ARF scar. Whether any 2018 / 2019 in situ points lie within it remains to be checked from their coordinates. Wu et al. publication

The paper, Table 4, source crosswalk, and data guide have been reviewed. Full observation CSVs for ORNL1903 / 2177 have not been obtained, so point-level matching remains open. Automated sensor data are kept separate from the manual field-activity count.

Team profile P21 →
Dissolved-silicon studyARF-083

Carey et al. silicon-cycling study: stream water collected by personnel using an extension pole and sampling bottle from a helicopter. Landings at every sampling point are not described.

Measurements / Samples Stream-water samples; dissolved silicon (DSi) and post-fire lateral export
Site Streams in and near ARF; the silicon study includes 22 burned and 23 unburned watersheds (45 watersheds across the full study)
Carey et al. (2019), Sect. 2.3, gives three sampling rounds and 22 burned plus 23 unburned watersheds. The supplementary material describes a 4 m sampling pole and 125 mL bottles. The relationship to Abbott's 42-watershed dataset still needs sample-level matching.
Nutrient / Water-chemistry studyARF-084

Abbott et al. nutrient-export study: manual stream-water collection during six rounds across 2017–2018, spanning snowmelt, peak growing season, and post-senescence. Entries are organized by study and year.

Measurements / Samples Stream-water samples; dissolved organic carbon, dissolved nitrogen, and inorganic nutrients for the study of lateral nutrient export
Site Twenty-one burned and 21 unburned watersheds in Abbott et al., within or near ARF (42 watersheds across the full study)
The combined 2017–2018 dataset covers 42 watersheds and six rounds. The author-uploaded workbook is “Abbott et al Tundra Burn Database.xlsx” (listed as 486.94 KB). Observation rows, site coordinates, and individual dates have not yet been read. Its site set and timing are retained separately from Carey's 45-watershed study.

Nutrient / Water-chemistry studyARF-085

Manual stream-water sampling continued to examine post-fire lateral nutrient loss. The combined 2017–2018 study had six rounds, using an extension pole from a helicopter. Landings at each point are not described.

Measurements / Samples Stream-water samples; dissolved organic carbon, dissolved nitrogen, and inorganic nutrients
Site Twenty-one burned and 21 unburned watersheds in Abbott et al.'s combined 2017–2018 study, within or near the fire area; individual sampling locations still need checking

PATCH-09 Latest year and the historical 2026 follow-up At that review, the latest core field year was 2025; 2026 uploads and a recent public field account were also noted. At that stage, 2026 remained a related lead; upload, publication, and visit dates were kept separately. An unconfirmed record means information is still open; it does not describe whether anyone visited.

7.2 Suggested additional fields

Field How to record it Purpose
Parent activity ID Enter established parent–child relationships; leave unknown values blank. Keep sub-tasks linked to their field campaigns.
Individual sampling dates／Date format Continuous interval, individual dates, campaign window, annual seasonal window, or unknown Preserve the original temporal precision when displaying start and end dates.
Original dataset ID and revision For example, knb-lter-arc.20139.1; retain the reviewed version. Distinguish dataset additions, revisions, and new fieldwork.
Source access Main text, supplementary table, original annual report, full metadata, metadata index, or observation-level data Show source access separately from raw CSV downloads.
Date / Spatial / Role review status Record separately rather than as a single score. An activity may have a known year, an unspecified PI, and a site described only in the text.
Has the original data file been obtained? Yes / No / Partial, with the entity or file named Describe data access separately from confirmation of the activity.
Last source-review date／Last note-revision date Retain both dates separately. Preserve earlier source-review dates alongside the later archive-compilation date.

Keep the existing Record ID、Team profile ID、Source IDs and Original inventory entries when changing display order. Activity, team-profile, and source IDs are stable cross-reference keys rather than chronological sequence numbers.

2. Separate components of Level 0 28

The paper combines elevation, temperature, and cryostratigraphic data, each with its own time structure. [R1][R2]

Acquisition dates Team label & Roles Main measurements / Parameters Status

29–31 July 2014 Jones and colleagues obtained the data through Kodiak Mapping Inc.; USGS contract G10PC00057. These acquisitions use the term “airborne LiDAR.” They had been proposed for inclusion in the discussion but were not yet written into the v3 files when this supplement was prepared. ARF-080 and later IDs had not yet been assigned at that stage.

2.2 Automated ground temperature: sampling frequency and summary period

Jones et al. (2024), “Ground temperature measurements”: ONSET HOBO U23-002 loggers were installed in July 2009, with external thermistors at 0.15 and 1.00 m. Hourly records were summarized as daily means and seasonal / Annual statistics. [R1]

The paper presents complete annual / Seasonal summaries for 2010–2022. The combined dataset's 2009–2023 title does not establish complete coverage of every depth and site, while the summary period also leaves possible 2023 raw records open. File-level valid dates and missing values remain to be checked.

2.3 Research roles

Jones led study design, LiDAR processing, spatial analysis, and fieldwork coordination. Kanevskiy, Shur, Veremeeva, and Jorgenson collected field data and led cryostratigraphy; Gaglioti led ground-temperature analysis. These are study-level contributions; visit-specific attendance is not fully listed. [R1]

3. Level 0 7: additional dataset, separate from manual fieldwork

The supplied report lists three package IDs and 2010–2013 coverage. A public data citation for the severely burned site's series was independently located:

Shaver, G. and Laundre, J. (2016). Summer soil temperature and moisture at the Anaktuvuk River Severely burned site from 2010 to 2013, version 2. DOI：10.6073/pasta/3094e3e293703580c95e17ddce51af65。[R4]

The supplied DOI 10.6073/pasta/14e1c3a85a6f32b1a62e45c3816f5874 resolved in that review to knb-lter-arc.10578.3. The EDI page was not fully accessible, so versions, sites, probes, and dates across 10578 / 10579 / 10580 remain to be checked in their complete metadata.

A suitable initial team label is “Shaver / Laundre (dataset authors / archive contacts).” Formal PI and installation / Maintenance roles remain open pending the respective EML or project records.

The report's details of three arrays, six probes, approximately 4–10 cm depths, and depth changes with frost heave / Disturbance remain labeled as information from the supplied database report, not independently rechecked field by field. The automated series is retained as a dataset reference; 2010–2013 manual soil collection or temperature visits would require separate records.

According to the supplied report, Level 0 14 and 31 archive different processing versions for the same three ARF burn-severity sites. Both sources are retained with shared site / Project links. Record overlap and variable comparability require coordinates, dates, processing versions, units, missing-value conventions, and QC checks. [R5; database-specific details are from the supplied report]

The Level 0 31 DOI 10.6073/pasta/005b8212ff751d8ca30be3350c89bae2 resolved in that review to knb-lter-arc.20115.1. This is one package entry within a multi-package collection; its complete metadata was not obtained. 5. Spatial selection

The supplied 1° buffer bounding box is a search area. Spatial roles are retained separately: burned points within the perimeter, internal unburned patches, and external controls. The main field timeline uses the first two, with external controls recorded separately.

ORNL2119's 26 transects include burned and unburned locations; a within-perimeter burned subset requires spatial selection. [R3]

Manual thaw probing near a tower remains fieldwork. Automated sensor operation is recorded separately from personnel visits.
